1.title: The Defender Portal, Notifications and Alert Correlation
1.text: Welcome to Module one: The Defender Portal, Notifications and Alert Correlation. It covers the exam area one. Manage a security operations environment. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Configure automation for Microsoft Defender X D R and Microsoft Sentinel: configure email notifications in Defender X D R, including incidents, actions and threat analytics. Configure alert notifications in Defender X D R, including tuning, suppression and correlation. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one. Manage a security operations environment (forty to forty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft S C-two hundred study guide and Microsoft Learn.

1.title: One portal, one incident queue
1.text: One portal, one incident queue. The figure shows this: The Defender portal: every workload and Sentinel feed one incident queue.

1.title: One portal, one incident queue, continued
1.text: One portal, one incident queue. The Microsoft Defender portal is where an analyst triages. Alerts from every Defender workload, and from Microsoft Sentinel once it is onboarded, are correlated into incidents in one queue. Portal path. Investigation and response, then Incidents and alerts, then Incidents. Alert. One detection from one product. Incident. A set of correlated alerts, the affected assets, investigations and evidence. Incident status. Active (default), In progress, Resolved. Severity. High, Medium, Low, Informational (starts at the highest alert severity). Owner. One user or group per incident. Exam tip: The unit of work is the incident, not the alert. Defender places each alert into a new or an existing incident by its own correlation logic.

1.title: Email notifications
1.text: Email notifications. Path: Settings, then Microsoft Defender X D R, then General, then Email notifications. Three tabs: Incidents, Actions, Threat analytics. You need the Manage security settings permission (basic permissions: Security Administrator or higher). Incidents. What the rule filters: Alert severity and device group scope. Key options: Send only one notification per incident; include the organization name; include a tenant-specific portal link. Actions. What the rule filters: Action source (manual, automated), the actions, device groups (all or selected), action status (completed, failed). Key options: Not supported for custom detections that contain response actions. Threat analytics. What the rule filters: All reports, or by report type or tag. Key options: At least one recipient.

1.title: Email notifications, continued
1.text: Email notifications. The incident wizard has five steps: Basics, Notification settings, Recipients (with Send test email), Review rule, Create rule. Exam tip: Actions notifications tell you when an automated or manual response action completed or failed. Incidents notifications tell you a new incident of a given severity exists. Pick the tab by the event.

1.title: How alerts become incidents: correlation and merging
1.text: How alerts become incidents: correlation and merging. Correlation. Defender adds an alert to a new or existing incident by proprietary correlation logic. Merge. The source incident moves into the target; the source is closed and tagged Redirected. Manual merge. Five incidents at a time. Not merged when. The source is closed; the assignees differ; the classifications or determinations differ; an entity limit would be exceeded; devices sit in different device groups (only when scoped device group correlation is on). The advanced feature Restrict correlation to within scoped device groups (Module two) stops incidents from combining devices of different device groups; it affects future correlation only. Exam tip: Different owners or different classifications block a merge. Align them first, then merge.

1.title: Alert tuning and suppression
1.text: Alert tuning and suppression. Alert suppression rule (Defender for Endpoint). Where: Settings, then Endpoints, then Rules, then Alert suppression. Effect: Suppresses matching alerts (for example a known-good line-of-business app); you can turn on, edit or delete the rule. Edit a suppression rule. Where: Same page. Effect: You can release alerts already suppressed. Defender for Identity tuning. Where: Alert tuning rules (Defender format). Effect: Replaces the old Excluded entities setting of the classic format. Suppress only proven false positives. A rule hides future alerts, so a wide rule can hide a real attack. Exam tip: A noisy alert from a trusted internal tool is solved with a suppression or tuning rule scoped to that tool, not by turning the detection off.

1.title: Microsoft Sentinel in the Defender portal
1.text: Microsoft Sentinel in the Defender portal. After onboarding, Sentinel works inside the Defender portal. Azure portal support ends after March thirty-one, twenty twenty-seven. The move has no extra cost. Incidents. Investigation and response, then Incidents and alerts, then Incidents. Logs. Investigation and response, then Hunting, then Advanced hunting. Workbooks, Hunting, Notebooks, my ter attack. Microsoft Sentinel, then Threat management. Content hub. Microsoft Sentinel, then Content management. Data connectors, Analytics, Watchlists, Automation. Microsoft Sentinel, then Configuration. Threat intelligence. Threat intelligence, then Intel management. Settings. System, then Settings, then Microsoft Sentinel.

1.title: Microsoft Sentinel in the Defender portal, continued
1.text: Microsoft Sentinel in the Defender portal. Differences that the exam may test: the incident queue is unified; Fusion is disabled; Microsoft incident creation rules are not supported; incidents created by A P I, playbook or by hand in Azure do not sync to Defender; a closed incident is not reopened by a new alert; bookmarks are not in Advanced hunting. Exam tip: Analytics rules and automation live under Microsoft Sentinel, then Configuration in the Defender portal.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A sock manager wants one email per incident whenever a high-severity incident is created, even if several alerts join it later. Which setting meets the requirement? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: An Incidents notification rule with one notification per incident enabled. The Incidents tab filters by severity and has the option to send only one notification per incident.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. The team wants an email when an automated device action fails to complete. Which notification tab should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The Actions tab, with automated as the source and failed as the status. Actions rules filter by source and by completed or failed status.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An analyst wants to be told whenever new ransomware reports appear in threat analytics. What should be configured? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A Threat analytics notification rule filtered by report type or tag. Threat analytics rules can cover all reports or filter by report type or tag.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An analyst merges two incidents, but the merge is refused. One incident is assigned to a user and the other is assigned to a different user. What is the reason? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Incidents with different assignees are not merged. Different assignees, different classifications or determinations, or a closed source incident block the merge.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A Sentinel engineer who used the Azure portal needs to open the analytics rules after onboarding to the Defender portal. Where are they? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Microsoft Sentinel, then Configuration, then Analytics. Data connectors, Analytics, Watchlists and Automation are under Microsoft Sentinel, then Configuration.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A user must create email notification rules but must hold the lowest role that allows it. Which permission is required? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Manage security settings, for example through Security Administrator. Email notification rules need the Manage security settings permission.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does the Actions notification tab report? Answer: Manual or automated response actions that completed or failed. Question two. What happens to the source incident after a merge? Answer: It is closed and tagged Redirected. Question three. How many incidents can be merged manually at a time? Answer: Five.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Where do you manage alert suppression rules for Defender for Endpoint? Answer: Settings, then Endpoints, then Rules, then Alert suppression. Question five. When does Azure portal support for Microsoft Sentinel end? Answer: After March thirty-one, twenty twenty-seven. Question six. Which Defender for Identity feature replaced the Excluded entities setting in the Defender format? Answer: Alert tuning rules.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Queue: Investigation and response, then Incidents and alerts, then Incidents. Notifications: Settings, then Microsoft Defender X D R, then General, then Email notifications: Incidents, Actions, Threat analytics. Permission: Manage security settings (Security Administrator or higher). Merge blockers: closed source, different assignees, different classification, entity limit, different device groups. Suppression: Settings, then Endpoints, then Rules, then Alert suppression. Sentinel paths: Configuration (analytics, connectors, automation), Threat management (hunting, workbooks).
